title: HubSpot vs SuiteCRM
comparison_markdown:
# HubSpot vs SuiteCRM (2026)

## Overview
HubSpot and SuiteCRM are two popular customer relationship management (CRM) tools that help businesses manage their sales, marketing, and customer service activities. This comparison is beneficial for small to medium-sized businesses and enterprises looking to switch from a proprietary CRM to a self-hosted, open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is to streamline CRM processes, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: HubSpot offers a free plan and several paid plans, while SuiteCRM is free and open-source.
* Data ownership: SuiteCRM allows users to have full ownership and control over their data, while HubSpot stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: HubSpot is generally easier to set up and use, while SuiteCRM requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: HubSpot is more scalable and can handle large volumes of data and users, while SuiteCRM may require more customization and configuration to scale.
* Integration: HubSpot has a more extensive library of integrations with third-party tools, while SuiteCRM has a more limited but still robust set of integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | HubSpot | SuiteCRM |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $15-$800+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $45-$1,200+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $180-$4,800+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**HubSpot:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Robust set of features and integrations
* Scalable and reliable
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data
**SuiteCRM:**
* Free and open-source
* Full control over data
* Customizable and flexible
* Self-hosting option
* Steeper learning curve

## When to Choose Each
HubSpot is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses that need a easy-to-use, scalable CRM solution with a wide range of integrations. It's also suitable for teams that don't require full control over their data and are willing to pay for a proprietary solution. SuiteCRM, on the other hand, is a good choice for businesses that require full control over their data, need a high degree of customization, and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining a self-hosted CRM solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from HubSpot in CSV format.
2. Set up a SuiteCRM instance on a self-hosted server.
3. Use the SuiteCRM import tool to import data from the CSV file.
4. Configure and customize SuiteCRM to meet specific business needs.
5. Test and verify that all data has been successfully migrated.

## Our Take
SuiteCRM is a production-ready CRM solution for most users, but it may require more technical expertise to set up and maintain. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that SuiteCRM's reporting and analytics capabilities are not as robust as HubSpot's. However, for businesses that require full control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into customization, SuiteCRM is a good choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with simple CRM needs and limited budget
* Teams of less than 10 users that don't require advanced features
* Businesses that require full control over their data and are willing to self-host
* Companies that need a high degree of customization and flexibility
* Organizations that don't require advanced reporting and analytics capabilities

## FAQ
### Is SuiteCRM free?
Yes, SuiteCRM is free and open-source.
### Can I self-host SuiteCRM?
Yes, SuiteCRM can be self-hosted on a server.
### Is HubSpot scalable?
Yes, HubSpot is scalable and can handle large volumes of data and users.
### Can I customize SuiteCRM?
Yes, SuiteCRM is highly customizable and flexible.
### Is SuiteCRM suitable for large enterprises?
Not yet, SuiteCRM may require more customization and configuration to scale for large enterprises.
meta_description: SuiteCRM, a free self-hosted CRM, offers full data control. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

## Overview
Mailchimp and Listmonk are two popular email marketing tools that help businesses manage their email campaigns and automate their marketing processes. This comparison is beneficial for businesses looking to switch from a proprietary email marketing platform to a self-hosted, open-source solution. The core use case for both tools is email marketing automation, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

* Cost: Mailchimp offers a free plan with limited features, while Listmonk is free and self-hosted, with no additional costs.
* Data ownership: Listmonk allows users to have full control over their data, while Mailchimp stores user data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Mailchimp has a more user-friendly interface and is easier to set up, while Listmonk requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Listmonk is highly scalable, as users can host it on their own servers, while Mailchimp has limitations on the number of subscribers and emails that can be sent.
* Integration difference: Listmonk has a more limited set of integrations with third-party tools, while Mailchimp has a wide range of integrations with popular services.

| Aspect | Mailchimp | Listmonk |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $13-$350+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |

* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of integrations with third-party tools
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data
* Can be expensive for large lists
**Listmonk:**
* Free and self-hosted
* Full control over data
* Highly scalable
* Limited integrations with third-party tools

Mailchimp is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses that need a user-friendly email marketing platform with a wide range of integrations. Listmonk, on the other hand, is a good choice for larger businesses or organizations that need a high degree of control over their data and want to reduce costs. It's also a good option for businesses that have the technical expertise to self-host their own email marketing platform.

## Migration Path

2. Set up your Listmonk instance on your own server.

We recommend switching to Listmonk if you have a large list and are comfortable with self-hosting your own email marketing platform.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with large email lists that want to reduce costs
* Medium-sized businesses that value control over their data

title: WordPress.com vs Ghost
comparison_markdown:
# WordPress.com vs Ghost

## Overview

Hosted blogging and website platform. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Ghost is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: WordPress.com costs Free / $4-$45+/month; Ghost is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: WordPress.com is Proprietary; Ghost is MIT
- **Data ownership**: Ghost can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Ghost eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Ghost has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | WordPress.com | Ghost |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $4-$45+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### WordPress.com

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Ghost

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [TryGhost/Ghost](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost) * ~47k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose WordPress.com if:** WordPress.com is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Ghost if:** Ghost is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from WordPress.com in its standard export format, review Ghost import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Ghost is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid WordPress.com tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Ghost instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for WordPress.com, switching to self-hosted Ghost will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on WordPress.com until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated WordPress.com paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Ghost free to use?
Yes. Ghost is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from WordPress.com to Ghost?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your WordPress.com data, follow the Ghost import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Ghost get regular updates?
Yes. Ghost has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Ghost without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Ghost development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [WordPress.com](https://wordpress.com) and [Ghost](https://ghost.org) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Ghost is a free, self-hosted alternative to WordPress.com. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

# Zendesk vs Zammad (2026)

## Overview
Zendesk and Zammad are two popular customer support platforms that help businesses manage their customer interactions. This comparison is beneficial for businesses looking to switch from a paid, proprietary solution to a free, self-hosted alternative. The core use case for both tools is to provide a centralized platform for customer support, and the key reason someone would switch is to reduce costs and gain more control over their data.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Zammad is free and self-hosted, while Zendesk charges per user per month.
* Data ownership: Zammad allows users to have full control over their data, while Zendesk stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Zammad requires more technical expertise to set up and configure, while Zendesk offers a more user-friendly interface.
* Scalability: Zendesk is more scalable and can handle larger volumes of customer interactions, while Zammad may require more configuration to scale.
* Feature difference: Zammad has a built-in knowledge base feature, while Zendesk charges extra for this feature.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Zendesk | Zammad |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $19-$115/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $950-$5,750/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $3,800-$23,000/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Zendesk
* Pros:
	+ User-friendly interface
	+ Scalable and reliable
	+ Integrates with many third-party apps
	+ Offers a wide range of features
	+ Good customer support
* Cons:
	+ Expensive, especially for large teams
	+ Limited customization options
	+ Data stored on proprietary servers
	+ Charges extra for some features
### Zammad
* Pros:
	+ Free and self-hosted
	+ Highly customizable
	+ Full control over data
	+ Open-source community
	+ Knowledge base feature included
* Cons:
	+ Requires technical expertise to set up and configure
	+ Limited scalability out of the box
	+ Not as many integrations with third-party apps
	+ Limited customer support
	+ Can be complex to use for non-technical users

## When to Choose Each
Zendesk is a good choice for large teams that need a scalable and reliable customer support platform, and are willing to pay for it. It's also a good choice for teams that need a wide range of features and integrations with third-party apps. On the other hand, Zammad is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that want a free, self-hosted solution and are willing to invest time and technical expertise to set it up and configure it. It's also a good choice for teams that want full control over their data and want to avoid proprietary solutions.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Zendesk in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a new Zammad instance and configure it to your needs.
3. Use the Zammad import tool to import your data from the CSV or JSON file.
4. Configure any necessary integrations with third-party apps.
5. Test your new Zammad instance to make sure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Zammad is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires technical expertise to set up and configure, and may have some scalability limitations. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Zammad uses a MySQL database, which can be complex to manage for large datasets. However, for small to medium-sized teams that want a free, self-hosted solution and are willing to invest time and technical expertise, Zammad is a good choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that don't need advanced features like AI-powered chatbots.
* Teams that want full control over their data and don't want to store it on proprietary servers.
* Teams that are currently using Zendesk's basic plan and don't need advanced features like multilingual support.
* Teams that are looking for a cost-effective solution and don't mind investing time and technical expertise to set up and configure Zammad.
* Teams that want a highly customizable solution and are willing to write custom code to extend Zammad's functionality.

## FAQ
### Is Zammad free?
Yes, Zammad is free and self-hosted. You only need to pay for the server costs.
### Can I migrate my data from Zendesk to Zammad?
Yes, you can export your data from Zendesk in CSV or JSON format and import it into Zammad using the Zammad import tool.
### Is Zammad scalable?
Zammad can be scalable, but it requires configuration and technical expertise to set up and manage a large dataset.

Yes, Zammad has a built-in knowledge base feature that is included in the free and self-hosted version.
